QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_2

question.text: A trader buys a GOI bond futures contract at Rs. 97.50 (quoted per Rs. 100 face value) and sells it at Rs. 98.20 after 30 days. If the contract is based on Rs. 2,00,000 face value, what is the profit per contract?

explanation.text: The Logic: GOI bond futures are quoted per Rs. 100 face value. Profit = (Sell price - Buy price) / 100 x Face value = (98.20 - 97.50) / 100 x 2,00,000 = 0.70 / 100 x 2,00,000 = Rs. 1,400. The Trap: Rs. 700 uses Rs. 1,00,000 face value. Rs. 2,800 doubles the correct figure. Rs. 1,000 uses an incorrect price differential. Note: Bond futures are priced per Rs. 100 face value, so price moves are scaled by face value. T-Bill futures use a different mechanic (100 minus discount yield, with a 0.25 factor), so do not apply this formula to T-Bill futures.
